reason: The numbers are right and the reading of them is wrong. Measured in chromium: on state=unfurl .b-chat is 560x341 at 700/701/720/768/1152/1279/1280/1440 (390 and 430 give a full-bleed 430), padding 28px 16px, with .b-bubble and .b-unfurl both 300px at x=chat+16 - so yes, 16px left and 244px right. But that 244px is not padding inside the card, it is the rest of the stage around it, and the 560 is not a property of the component at all: shell.css names exactly four media and sets [data-medium="card"] .tl-stage { max-width: 560px }, and body carries data-medium="card" on unfurl - the same mechanism that gives the phone states 390 and print 794 (A4 at 96dpi). .b-chat fills its stage exactly, edge to edge, like every other state fills its own. The finding calls it a 'plate'; it is not one. The plate is .b-chatPlate - the border and 12px radius - and unfurl deliberately does not carry that class. In unfurl .b-chat is the chat client's own white surface, which is why the CSS comment above it reads 'LITERAL, not laddered: the chat app is somebody else's surface and it is light whatever ground we chose.' The card renders at the 300px a real client draws it, left-aligned, as a received message. The publish comparison is a category error, not a matched pair: there the same card() is mounted as a specimen under the label 'What lands in the message', on a bordered plate that correctly hugs it (320 around 286 at 1440; 350 around 300 at 390); here it is shown in situ in a thread, and a thread is wider than the message in it. The proposed fix makes it worse on both routes. Route one - width:fit-content; max-width:332px; margin-inline:auto - would make the chat surface 332px at desk widths, NARROWER than the same surface at 390 (430px measured), so the imitated window would shrink as the viewport grows; and it deletes the only cue in the frame that says this is somebody else's app rather than ours - a message that does not fill its window. A card hugged by 16px of white on all four sides reads as a specimen on a mount, which is precisely what publish already does one state earlier; doing it twice loses the distinction between 'the asset' and 'the asset in the wild'. Route two - 528px bubble and card - the finding itself concedes is wrong, and it is: no chat client draws a 528px link preview, so it would falsify the one state whose whole job is to be true to the medium. The remaining charge, 'the brightest rectangle in the fourteen-state set and 44% of it empty', is an argument for adding chat chrome or a border, not for the fix proposed, and the grey bubble already does that work: it is the thing that reads the white as a window.
